mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer demand and corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 6% and then rises above 6% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods when UNRATE exceeds 6% for three months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) for two consecutive quarters signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenues and earnings, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of two consecutive quarterly declines in RSAFS (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 25 basis point or greater increase in the federal funds rate over a single month signals a tightening monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by 0.25% or more in a single month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of a single-month 25bp FEDFUNDS increase (t-test p > 0.05).
